Hannah — thanks for the summary and sorry for the rapid-fire questions. A few clarifications from our side so Ben and Jordan can target answers: 

- For logs: we separate "audit" logs (security events, admin actions) from "application" logs (requests, prompts). Audit logs need 12 months retention for our regulator; application logs can be shorter. Can you confirm default and extended retention for both categories?
- Backups/snapshots: when you say "backup retention," does that include incremental snapshots that might contain PII? Under GDPR we need a clear timeline for when a DSR-triggered deletion will propagate to backups and snapshots.
- Deletion: we generally require an explanation of the deletion workflow (soft delete + purge) and an estimated timeline — for example: 30d soft retention, then 60d pending snapshot pruning, final irrevocable deletion at 90d. Are those numbers close to Redwood's practice or do you have different defaults?

We prefer the vendor questionnaire as an editable Google Sheet — our legal/security team will collaborate there. Target reviewers: myself (security lead) + Emily Park (BlueArc Legal). Timeline: we'd like completed questionnaire and SOC 2 evidence by COB Jan 15 so legal can triage before Jan 18.

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Alex — thanks, this is helpful. Below are concrete answers and links to the artifacts we've attached. I kept this focused so your legal/security reviewers can pick what they need.

1) SOC 2 / compliance posture
- Redwood: SOC 2 Type II report (rolling 12-month window), most recent attestation: 2025 audit cycle. Certificate and short summary attached (SOC2-Cert-2025.pdf).
- HIPAA: Redwood offers a Business Associate Agreement for customers with PHI; our controls map to common HIPAA requirements. We do not provide PHI processing by default unless covered by a BAA and dedicated configuration.
- GDPR: We support DSR workflows (export + delete). Our product supports regional routing and can be configured to keep customer data in-region for EU customers.

2) Log retention (defaults and extensions)
- Application logs (request-level): default retention 90 days (hosted). Optional add-on: 365 days (paid).
- Audit/security logs: default retention 365 days. Can be extended to multiyear archival via our compliance add-on (S3 archival).
- Logs used for debugging (short-term caches/rolling buffers) are 7 days by default and not intended for audit.

3) Backups & snapshots (how they relate to DSR/deletion)
- Snapshot retention (hosted): default snapshot lifecycle is 30 days for daily snapshots and 7 days for incremental hourly snapshots; these are encrypted at rest with customer-data separation.
- For Dedicated customers, snapshot retention is configurable — typical commits go to 90 days + optional long-term archive.
- DSR propagation: when a DSR deletion request is honored, we logically delete the primary records immediately and mark related backups/snapshots for purge. Pragmatically, immutable snapshot contents may persist for the configured snapshot window; we run scheduled snapshot pruning that will remove marked data during the next prune cycle.
- Typical timeline we operate on (hosted default):
  * Immediate logical deletion on the primary store at time 0.
  * Soft-delete marker retained for 30 days (customer-visible restore window).
  * Snapshot pruning runs daily and will remove marked data according to snapshot retention windows; in hosted default this leads to physical removal within ~30-60 days depending on snapshot timing.
  * Final physical purge from all our storage tiers typically completes within 90 days for hosted customers unless longer retention was purchased.

4) Restore targets (RTO / RPO)
- Hosted (standard): RTO "best effort" under 24 hours for full restore from 30-day snapshot; RPO up to 24 hours for daily snapshots.
- Dedicated (SLA-backed): typical RTO < 4 hours, RPO < 15 minutes when cross-region replication is enabled (dedicated config).

5) Encryption, access controls, and evidence
- All data at rest is encrypted (AES-256) and keys are managed via our KMS (customer-managed keys available for Dedicated/Private).
- Access to backups and audit logs is restricted by RBAC and logged. We can provide canned access logs for a given time window upon request.

Attachments included: SOC2-Cert-2025.pdf, data-retention-schema_v2.pdf (one-page lifecycle diagram). Also attaching a populated Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx (editable).
